title: Influencer marketing still works, it just stopped being cheap: why UGC is the window
summary: Jake argues influencer marketing still works but CPMs have spiked across all creator tiers because everyone copied the Cal AI playbook, killing margins. He recommends shifting to UGC (not yet exhausted or overpriced), sourcing via SideShift or Trybe, and moving Q4 effort into organic since paid CPMs spike. He lists funnel prerequisites UGC needs to convert.

principles.text: Influencer marketing still works; the problem is price. CPMs rose while creator quality and RPMs stayed flat.
principles.quote: Influencer marketing didn't stop working. It just stopped being cheap.

principles.text: When a profitable playbook gets copied, everyone bids for the same creators and creators reprice, killing margins.
principles.quote: People saw what we were doing (and other profitable brands too) to scale our operations and decided influencer marketing was the move.

principles.text: Move into the channel that isn't yet exhausted or overpriced. UGC is where influencer marketing was a couple of years ago.
principles.quote: UGC hasn't been exhausted YET and it's not overpriced YET.

principles.text: Source UGC creators via performance-based pay (Trybe) or abundant supply (SideShift), plus a VA doing manual outreach.
principles.quote: Creators make the content with nothing paid upfront, you run it as an ad, and they take a percentage of the spend on the video they made (you pay out only on performance).

principles.text: Don't try to outbid in Q4 paid ads; accept slower paid scaling for consumer apps and invest in organic channels.
principles.quote: My advice is to not try to outbid anybody.

principles.text: UGC only works if fundamentals are in place: angles, scripts, a product understood in seconds, test budget, and an optimized funnel.
